# Comments

## [File Header](https://github.com/dynamotn/bash-coding-style/blob/main/README.md#file-header)

- ✔️ SHOULD: Include a comment at the beginning of the file that concisely explains the purpose or content of the file. However, do not include comments before the shebang line <kbd>BSG024</kbd>
- ✔️ SHOULD: Use [sh-docs](https://github.com/dynamotn/sh-docs) ([GitLab](https://gitlab.com/dynamo-tools/sh-docs)) format includes: `@file`, `@brief`, `@description` to explain the file. (custom) <kbd>BSG020</kbd>
- ⚠️ CONSIDER: Name the license of a distributed script with `# SPDX-License-Identifier: <id>`, not a license paragraph <kbd>BSG149</kbd>

## [Function Comments](https://github.com/dynamotn/bash-coding-style/blob/main/README.md#function-comments)

- ✔️ SHOULD: Use [sh-docs](https://github.com/dynamotn/sh-docs) ([GitLab](https://gitlab.com/dynamo-tools/sh-docs)) format to explain the function. (custom) <kbd>BSG021</kbd> <kbd>BSG022</kbd>

## [Implementation Comments](https://github.com/dynamotn/bash-coding-style/blob/main/README.md#implementation-comments)

- ✔️ SHOULD: Add comments to code that is tricky, has significant meaning, or requires attention
- ✔️ SHOULD: Keep comments short and easy to understand whenever possible
- ⚠️ CONSIDER: If a brief explanation is not sufficient, consider providing detailed background information

## [TODO Comments](https://github.com/dynamotn/bash-coding-style/blob/main/README.md#todo-comments)

- ✔️ SHOULD: Consider using TODO comments
- ❌ AVOID: Do not include the name of the person who wrote the TODO comment. (custom) <kbd>BSG023</kbd>

## [Commented-out Code](https://github.com/dynamotn/bash-coding-style/blob/main/README.md#commented-out-code)

- ⚠️ CONSIDER: Delete code instead of commenting it out; git keeps the old version. (custom) <kbd>BSG144</kbd>
- ✔️ SHOULD: When a line has to stay switched off for now, put a TODO above it that says why and when it comes back
- ✔️ SHOULD: Show example code in an shdoc `@example`, not as loose comment lines
